name: reference_pipe
title: Reference pipe model
summary: A water pipe assembled from an adiabatic pressure-drop model and an isobaric heat-gain model. The friction factor is the Colebrook equation; the heat gain is an epsilon-NTU balance with fixed convection coefficients.

verification.summary: Against the stored solution of Reference pipe model JL080103.EES: 54 common variables, 4 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 2. Maximum relative difference 1.538e-03 on c_p_pipe_02 (EES 4195.960667, CoolSolve 4202.424522 J/(kg·K)). C_dot_pipe_02, NTU_pipe_02 and epsilon_pipe_02 follow from that cp. Pressure drop, heat gain and outlet temperature stay within rtol 0.001.
verification.reference: EES stored solution in Reference pipe model JL080103.EES (54 variables)
verification.notes: The four variables above rtol 0.001 are one CoolProp/EES specific-heat difference at the heat-gain inlet. AU_pipe_02 matches the stored 19.81394555 W/K, so NTU = AU/C_dot and epsilon = 1-exp(-NTU) follow the cp ratio. Q_dot_pipe is 474.3061201 W against 474.3041201 W (rel 4.22e-06). t_ex_pipe is 6.118393565 °C against 6.118581062 °C (rel 3.06e-05). DELTAp_pipe_01 is 23439.81082 Pa against 23440.45337 Pa (rel 2.74e-05); the viscosity difference is 4.75e-04. Stored enthalpy is already in J/kg (blank unit, 25417.30434; CoolSolve 25421.65865 J/kg, rel 1.71e-04); --ees-units was not used. Only in CoolSolve: pi, and t_ex_pipe_01, which is absent from the extracted variable list and equals t_su_pipe_02. The .sol labels v_pipe_01 as kg/m^3; the value is the specific volume in m^3/kg. With .initials the solve takes 8 iterations; without them, 122 iterations, the same root. abs(C_pipe_01) does not open a second root because the velocity follows from the positive mass flow.
